text:
every so often he comes back

to me,

there in his bed, blind,

being slowly consumed,

the little bulldog,

the nurses prowling, running

the curtains, the blinds, the sheets.

seeing whether he was still alive.

the boy from Colorado.

the courage of American Mercury.

the bad Catholic boy of Mencken.

who went to Hollywood.

and lay down on its shore.

consuming himself, consuming himself, consuming himself,

until he was gone.

he never knew he would be famous.

i wonder if he would have

cared.

i think he would.


John, this is your big moment.

you entered the books of

eternity

there beside Dostoevsky,

Tolstoy, and your little

Sherwood Anderson


I told you so.


and you said

“you wouldn’t shit on an old blind man,

would you?”

ah, there’s no need for that,

bulldog.

translation.title: Every So Often He Comes Back...
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Charles Bukowski. Lowercase presentation, repetitions, quoted speech, and stanza spacing are preserved.
